summary: The Markdown color authority now exposes every Pantone COY identity, resolves safe canonical aliases with collision evidence, carries parsed provenance and explicit local extensions, and owns typed runtime neutral/state/chrome defaults consumed by core token paths.
decisions: Keep the 87 authored card API stable and generate a checksum-bound visible index for all 29 Pantone COY Semantic IDs from the embedded payload.
Resolve exact labels and Semantic IDs before aliases; register color_name only when unique, and retain explicit two-identity evidence for Cerulean and Marsala.
Treat numeric card citations as aliases for real ColorReference IDs and expose resolved provenance on every parsed card.
Align Hunter Green and Teal Blue with their Semantic OS families and bind Rose Quartz to its Pantone COY identity.
Represent Dark Salmon and Blanched Almond as named local ColorKeyword extensions with a local ColorReference plus contains, cites, and spectrum-topic edges without mutating the upstream payload.
Store runtime neutral, state, chrome, and dark-derivation values in a checksum-verified typed Markdown policy; keep them distinct from ColorKeyword nodes and let explicit project roles win.
Fail closed when the default Markdown authority loses its runtime policy; custom card references without a policy explicitly inherit the packaged default policy.

Lock the manual role identity and HEX values for the seven affected real projects (lattice, quill, broadside, lattice-dash, panel-pop, orchard, and world-cup-hub) against the repository-local Markdown authority.

gate_results.evidence: Wheel contained resources/color-reference.md; from /tmp the package fallback loaded 87 cards, 29 COY identities, the verified runtime policy, and the merged 361-node/1235-edge runtime ontology.

risks: The embedded Semantic OS payload intentionally remains 358 nodes and 1227 edges; the local runtime overlay is 361 nodes and 1235 edges, so consumers must not compare those two layers as if they were the same artifact.

The generated COY identity table is an index rather than 29 additional authored cards; consumers that need complete visible identity coverage should use color_index or pantone_coy_index instead of assuming colors contains generated rows.
